summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Thatchathon Attarung pursued a Ph.D. in Linguistics at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (2024–2026). In 2024, they served as Secretary to the Dean's Office there and as Associate Editor of the Journal of Applied Humanities Studies.
Theo Murray works in the fields of Buddhist and religious studies. As of 2026, he is a PhD candidate and student at the Australian National University.

Theodoor Paul Galestin was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University (1927–1936) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom, later serving as extraordinary professor at the University of Amsterdam (1945–1957) and professor at Leiden University (1957–1977).

Theodor Aufrecht worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and Karl Lachmann, and earned his Ph.D. from Halle-Wittenberg. He was a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875) and University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Baader was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Bern and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Münster (1910–1913), where he became Privatdozent in 1920 before serving as professor at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1944).

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Theodor Baunack studied at Leipzig under Georg Curtius and Hermann Brockhaus (1880), and earned his Ph.D. at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (1882–1884). In 1889, he taught at the Alte Nikolaischule.

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who completed his education, Ph.D., and Habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there, serving as Privatdozent from 1834, Lehrmeister in 1848, and Ordinarius from 1862 to 1881.

Theodor Bloch was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig and studied under Georg Bühler and John Marshall. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig in 1896, joined the Archaeological Survey of India (1900), and read at Calcutta (~1908–1909).

Theodor Duka was an active figure in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and St George's, University of London, later serving as an assistant surgeon and Surgeon-Lieutenant-Colonel in the Bengal Army (1854–1874) and Vice-President of the British and Foreign Bible Society.

Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his PhD at Königsberg and studied at Bonn and with Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London and University of London (1851–1872) and presided over the Philological Society.

Theodor Korsch was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov at Moscow State University, earning his Ph.D. there. He taught at Moscow State University as Privatdozent and extraordinary professor, as well as at Odesa University and Lazarev Institute.

Theodor Mommsen was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Kiel University. He held academic posts at Leipzig, Zurich, Breslau, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and Frederick William University Berlin (1861–1885).

Theodor Nöldeke specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Heinrich Ewald, completing his Ph.D. and Habilitation, before holding professorships at Kiel (1864–1872) and Strasbourg (1872–1906).
Theodor Schultze was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied law at Kiel University from around 1843 to 1847 and also studied at Frederick William University Berlin.

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen (Ph.D.), and Oxford, and completed his Habilitation at Greifswald. He served as professor at Greifswald (1883) and ao. Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).
Theodor von Oppolzer studied at the University of Vienna from around 1859 to 1865. He subsequently held a post at the University of Vienna from around 1866 until 1886.

Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at Yale and Princeton, later serving as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and as president of the American Oriental Society.

Theodore Riccardi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Columbia University, attested in 1974–1976 and 1990, and served as a Guest Editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society in 1989.

Theodore Riccardi Jr. is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He spent his career at Columbia University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2014 and as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Theodore Stcherbatsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi, and was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1927–1931).
